strategy.label: Ocean Protection Council, Statewide Microplastics Strategy (2022)

gpl.name: Global Plastic Laws
gpl.disclaimer: The Global Plastic Laws Database is an educational and research resource and should not be regarded as fully comprehensive or completely up to date for legal purposes.

actions.summary: Carry out the statewide rule that single-use foodware and condiments are handed out only on request (AB 1276, 2021).
Encourage state purchasing and service contracts to require reusable foodware where feasible and cut the state's use of single-use foodware.
Adopt comprehensive statewide goals for plastic source reduction, reuse and refill.
Prohibit the sale and distribution of expanded polystyrene foodware and packaging.
Extend the AB 888 (2015) microbead ban to microplastics intentionally added to products such as cosmetics, detergents and cleaning products.
Prohibit single-use tobacco products that add to plastic pollution, including cigarette filters, e-cigarettes, plastic cigar tips and unrecyclable packaging.
Identify extended producer responsibility (EPR) approaches for recycling or disposing of plastic packaging and foodware.
Promote or require ENERGY STAR condenser dryers and washing machines that filter to 100 microns or smaller, with rebates or other incentives for retrofits and purchases.
Bring together industries (such as tires, textiles, agriculture, foodware and packaging, fisheries and aquaculture) and scientists to find alternatives and sector-specific prevention strategies.
Prioritise low impact development (LID) green-infrastructure retrofits on existing development that loads microplastics to receiving waters.
Evaluate how well LID structural best management practices remove microplastics, and identify sites where LID should be required.
Depending on 2A.2.2 findings, consider LID requirements for new and redevelopment projects in water quality permits, local coastal programs and coastal development permits.
Prioritise compliance assurance and enforcement of discharge prohibitions for preproduction plastic pellets (nurdles).
Prioritise trash receptacles and trash services at hot spots (busy beaches, recreation areas, encampments near waterways) outside the statewide Trash Provisions.
Implement the statewide Trash Provisions and meet the final deadline of no trash in state surface waters.
Building on wastewater-treatment removal studies, further promote recycling of tertiary-treated wastewater that would otherwise go to the ocean.
After the SCCWRP treatment-efficacy study, develop microplastic reduction strategies and monitoring recommendations for each level of wastewater treatment.
Work with California Native American Tribes on outreach, monitoring and immediate plastic and microplastic reduction.
Engage underserved communities and those burdened by environmental injustice in decisions, and pursue immediate solutions with them.
Run a public awareness campaign on microplastic pollution that supports behaviour, policy and systemic change.
Promote K-12 education on microplastic sources, impacts and solutions through curricula, standards and teacher training.
Promote industry engagement and outreach on sector-specific microplastic prevention strategies.
